chunks: The venerable Sheikh Abu Ja'far recited to us, attributed to one of them:

"The wise scholar is the son of himself, His kind of knowledge has made him needless of his lineage. How vast is the difference between one whom you honor for the sake of others, And one whom you honor for his own sake."

key_terms.ابن نفسه: Son of himself: a self-made person, one whose merit comes from personal achievement rather than lineage
key_terms.العالم العاقل: The wise scholar: one who combines knowledge (ilm) with intellect (aql)
key_terms.جنس علمه: The kind/genus of his knowledge: the nature and quality of his learning

ai.seo_question: What does Islamic poetry say about the value of knowledge versus lineage?
ai.summary: This poetic verse, recited in the teaching assembly (majlis) of Sheikh al-Tusi on Tuesday the 19th of Muharram 368 AH, extols the self-made scholar whose personal knowledge and intellect make him independent of ancestral nobility. The contrast is drawn between someone honored only due to family connections and one honored for genuine personal merit. In the scholarly circles of Shia learning, this poem would have resonated as an encouragement to pursue knowledge as the truest source of honor.
